title: Words to live by? - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Cowen quotes The Economist cataloguing a year of record US capital-markets deals — SpaceX's IPO, OpenAI's private round, Amazon's bond, Nvidia's buyback, the EA LBO, Paramount-WBD junk bonds — arguing American finance is a machine so large and flexible it steamrollers scandals like First Brands and Situational Awareness.

insights.claim: In the past year US markets absorbed the largest-ever IPO (SpaceX), largest equity raise by a public company (Google) and by a foreign firm (SK Hynix), and the largest private-funding round (OpenAI).
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Unprecedented equity supply concentrated in AI/space names tests market absorption capacity — a signal of peak-cycle issuance.
insights.locator: In the past year American markets

insights.claim: Nvidia ran a record-breaking stock-buyback programme and Berkshire Hathaway held a record cash pile over the past year.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Juxtaposition of AI-winner buybacks with Buffett's record cash hoard is a positioning signal on valuations.
insights.locator: In the past year American markets

insights.claim: Vanguard launched/hit the first $1 trillion ETF.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.locator: In the past year American markets

insights.claim: The past year saw the largest private-debt deal (Broadcom), most of the biggest bond issue in history (Amazon), and the largest-ever leveraged buyout (Electronic Arts).
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: AI capex and LBO financing are pushing debt markets to record sizes — rising leverage risk in hyperscaler/semis complex.
insights.locator: In the past year American markets

insights.claim: The Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery merger led to the largest-ever junk-bond offering, beating a record set only a week earlier by SoftBank.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Back-to-back record high-yield deals signal very loose credit conditions.
insights.quote: the largest ever junk-bond offering, beating a record set only last week (SoftBank)
insights.locator: In the past year American markets

insights.claim: Enormous mergers occurred in railways (Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern), utilities (NextEra and Dominion Energy) and media (Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery).
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Consolidation wave spans infrastructure-like sectors; utility M&A tied to power demand.
insights.locator: In the past year American markets

insights.claim: New markets have been created out of thin air for compute, while prediction markets have become much bigger.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Compute as a tradable commodity and scaling prediction markets are emerging asset classes.
insights.quote: New markets have been created out of thin air (for compute) or become much bigger (for predictions)
insights.locator: In the past year American markets

insights.claim: Major corporate scandals (First Brands) and hedge-fund blow-ups (Situational Awareness) that once would have preoccupied investors for months are being steamrollered by the 'relentless, totalising and extraordinarily flexible' American finance machine.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Markets are shrugging off credit and fund-blowup warnings — a resilience story that can also read as complacency risk.
insights.quote: are steamrollered by the relentless, totalising and extraordinarily flexible machine that is American finance
insights.locator: In the past year American markets

insights.claim: Tyler Cowen endorses The Economist's passage on record-breaking US finance as excellent, framing it as 'words to live by'.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Cowen shares the view that US capital-markets depth is a durable advantage.
insights.locator: An excellent passage, from The Economist.
